listing.style: Sea Ranch–inspired contemporary, built 1976 (MLS style: Other; Montclair)
listing.description: Set on approximately one-third of an acre just 2 minutes from the 13, in the Oakland Hills, this architecturally distinctive, Sea Ranch–inspired home celebrates the relationship between architecture and nature. Dramatic angles, soaring ceilings, natural wood, and expansive windows create spaces that feel both intimate and expansive, with extraordinary light that shifts throughout the day. Rooted in Northern California's architectural tradition of responding to the landscape rather than imposing upon it, the home embraces its hillside setting. Angular rooflines, varied ceiling heights, and warm natural materials give the interiors a sculptural quality, while skylights and large windows invite the surrounding trees, greenery, and sky into everyday life. The two bedroom, two bathroom home features an open, flowing living and dining area with a wonderful sense of volume and connection between spaces. An updated kitchen and beautifully refreshed bathrooms bring contemporary comfort while respecting the home's architectural character. Southwest-facing windows capture gorgeous afternoon light and the soft pink glow of  sunsets. On rainy days, a fire in the fireplace brings warmth and intimacy to the soaring living spaces, with the surrounding trees and changing weather providing an ever-present connection to nature. Outside, a series of terraced gardens and inviting outdoor spaces extend the living experience into the hillside. Established planting areas offer opportunities to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers, while decks and garden retreats provide places for dining, entertaining, or quiet contemplation. A private sauna and plunge pool create a wonderful opportunity for relaxation and renewal, surrounded by the beauty and tranquility of the natural setting. A detached, unpermitted structure  offers a separate space for working or creative pursuits. Wildlife is part of the daily experience, from deer and foxes moving through the hillside to hawks overhead and owls calling in the evening. Despite its remarkable privacy, the home is part of a warm, welcoming neighborhood with wonderful longtime neighbors and a genuine sense of community. With its extraordinary light, expressive architecture, natural materials, and deep connection to the landscape, 318 Capricorn offers a distinctive expression of Northern California living.

condition.note: Quality kitchen/bath updates (p_12, p_22, p_32), staged with disclosed digital alteration (p_02, p_07, p_11); 1976 shell, comp-shingle roof serviceable (p_44), some weathered shingle staining (p_46).

verdict: This house IS architecture-and-light over view: a sculptural 1976 Sea Ranch–style shed contemporary tucked into a wooded Montclair bowl, with exceptional natural light, a genuinely updated Wolf kitchen and baths, and a rare sauna + plunge-pool + detached-studio compound. The trade-offs are real: no living-level water view despite the marketing's Bay Bridge shot, 1,655 sf sliced across five split levels with the primary bath a flight away from the primary bedroom, a steep mostly-unusable upslope lot, and the full Oakland-hills fire burden — combustible cedar-shingle siding, wood decks, and Very High FHSZ insurance exposure. For a solo buyer working from home who values character, light, and privacy over panorama, it is a strong, honestly-marketed candidate at $541/sf.
